variants: Who was Joseph Morris?
What is a Morrisite?
Tell me about the Morrisites

paragraphs.text: The Morrisites were followers of Joseph Morris, an English convert to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints who began recording revelations in Utah in the late 1850s. He organized his own church at South Weber on April 6, 1861, and his followers gathered at Kington Fort on the Weber River.

In June 1862 a territorial posse besieged the fort for three days. Morris was killed at the surrender, and the movement scattered: to Soda Springs, Idaho; Carson Valley, Nevada, and San Francisco; Omaha and Council Bluffs; William W. Davies's community near Walla Walla; and the Deer Lodge Valley in Montana, where the last organized Morrisite church lasted until George Johnson's death in 1954.

q: What happened at Kington Fort in June 1862?
variants: What was the Morrisite War?
Tell me about the siege of Kington Fort
Why did the posse attack the Morrisites?

paragraphs.text: The "Morrisite War" is the common name for the three-day siege of Morris's followers at Kington Fort, South Weber, by a territorial posse under Robert T. Burton. It began over writs for the arrest of Morris and other leaders after three departing members were brought back to the fort and held; the fort refused to answer the writs.

The posse arrived on June 13, 1862, and the first cannon ball killed two women. On Sunday, June 15, a white flag went up; Morris was killed at the surrender, and John Banks, wounded, died that evening. Two posse men were killed, Jared Smith and Peter Wahler. The accounts disagree on the Morrisite dead, and no list has been checked against all the sources.

quotes.text: killed two women & wounded a third

variants: How many people were killed in the Morrisite War?
How did Joseph Morris die?
Who killed Joseph Morris?

paragraphs.text: Accounts differ on the number of dead and on some of their names. Morris was killed at the surrender and John Banks died in custody that evening. Two women were killed by the first cannon shot on June 13, and Isabella Bowman was one of two Morrisite women killed during the surrender. On the posse side, Jared Smith and Peter Wahler were killed.

A posse member, John G. Chambers, wrote that at the surrender "the Colonel with his aides killed Morris & Banks." Robert T. Burton was indicted for Isabella Bowman's death and tried in 1879, and acquitted. No list of the dead checked against all the sources exists.

q: Was my ancestor a Morrisite? How can I find out?
variants: How do I find a Morrisite ancestor?
Is my family on the roll?
How can I tell if my ancestor was a member?

paragraphs.text: Start with the name index, which lists everyone on the 1861–62 roll and everyone else the sources name, with links to every place the guide mentions them. Try other spellings: clerks spelled Danish, Swedish, Welsh and English names as they heard them.

For people in Montana after 1862, most of whom are not on the roll, see the register of Montana Morrisites. FamilySearch links marked "probable" are likely but not certain, and Family Tree is shared and editable, so check its sources before relying on it. The roll itself is not complete: its compiler wrote that many baptized were never recorded.

q: What is the roll of membership?
variants: How many people joined Joseph Morris?
How many Morrisites were there?

paragraphs.text: The roll of membership lists 430 people baptized into Morris's church in 1861–62, printed in San Francisco by George S. Dove & Co. in 1886. It is not complete: its compiler wrote that many baptized were never recorded, and Josiah D. Price counted himself the "431st person" in the church.

variants: What did Morris teach about plural marriage?
Were the Morrisites polygamists?

paragraphs.text: Later writers often describe Morris as an opponent of plural marriage, while Kirk Watson's introduction argues that he accepted it as a celestial principle. Morris's own article of June 4, 1861, says the law of many wives was given for this life, "not being a celestial law." An angel's testimony through Morris in June 1862 calls polygamy true "in its proper time and place," and it was not practiced at Kington Fort (Watson).

q: Did Joseph Morris predict the date of the Second Coming?
variants: When did the Morrisites expect Christ to come?
Did Morris set dates for the coming of Christ?
Did the Morrisites expect the end of the world?

paragraphs.text: Yes. The guide's timeline sets out every moment the sources record when the time of Christ's coming was set, tied to a condition, refused, or explained after it passed. The best known is the revelation of December 30, 1861, which promised that Christ would come "to-morrow morning" if those present consecrated all their property.
Later leaders differed: George Williams declined to set a date, while in Montana William James looked to 1891, probably following a statement of Joseph Smith that Orson Pratt printed.

q: What is the Lord's House at Racetrack?
variants: Where is the Morrisite church in Montana?
Does the Morrisite church building still stand?
Racetrack church

paragraphs.text: The Lord's House is the Montana Morrisites' wood-frame church near Racetrack, built in 1878–79 on Andrew Hendrikson's land and dedicated on August 9, 1879. George Williams called it "a Temple in miniature and place of worship for the faithful."
It still stands on private land at Racetrack, about 8 miles south of Deer Lodge, and is the last Morrisite church standing.

q: When did the Montana Morrisite church end?
variants: Is there a Morrisite church today?
When did the Morrisites disband?
Are there still Morrisites?

paragraphs.text: George Johnson presided at the Lord's House until shortly before his death on April 29, 1954. Anderson dates the end of the church to his death, after which the Lord's House was boarded up; surviving Morrisites still gathered there on August 9, 1969, though by then the gatherings were more social than religious.

Utah State University's descriptions say the church formally disbanded in 1969, and Henry Hendrickson told an interviewer in 1962 that it faded about 1919–20. The two later dates may describe different things, and no record made at the time has been found for what, if anything, formally ended the church.

variants: Who ordained Morris?
Was Joseph Morris ordained?
Where did Morris get his priesthood?
What priesthood did Joseph Morris hold?
Was Morris a high priest?

paragraphs.text: Before he founded his own church, Joseph Morris was a Latter-day Saint high priest. The membership record of the High Priests Quorum enters a Joseph Morris as ordained at Great Salt Lake City on July 5, 1854, by J. L. Haywood (probably Heywood) and A. Hoagland, and enrolled in the quorum the same day. Kirk Watson found the entry.

Morris himself later wrote that he had been ordained "to the office of a high priest" in the High Priests' Quorum at Great Salt Lake City, and said that this only acknowledged an ordination he had first received in heaven.

q: Who was George Williams, the Prophet Cainan?
variants: Who was Cainan?
Who led the Morrisites after Morris?

paragraphs.text: George Williams, born February 14, 1814, at Thorpe, Surrey, claimed to be Morris's successor and led the church that gathered in the Deer Lodge Valley, Montana, from the late 1860s. He left America for England about January 1869 and led by letter from there. In 1879 he told the Montana Saints that the region where they lived was "the Sides of the North"; he set no date for the Lord's coming.

q: Who was the Walla Walla Jesus?
variants: Who was William W. Davies?
What was the Kingdom of Heaven at Walla Walla?

paragraphs.text: "Walla Walla Jesus" is a later popular name for Arthur Davies (1868–1880), son of William W. Davies. Davies said that on the eighth day after the boy's birth he proclaimed the Messiah come again in him. The boy and his younger brother David both died of diphtheria in February 1880.

variants: What scripture did the Morrisites use?
Where can I read Morris's revelations?

paragraphs.text: The Spirit Prevails holds Joseph Morris's revelations, articles and letters, recorded from 1857 to 1862 and published after his death by his follower George S. Dove in 1886. It holds more than 300 revelations, and for his followers it was scripture. Free scans are on the Internet Archive and Google Books.

q: Did Morrisites join the RLDS Church?
variants: Did Morrisites become Josephites?
What happened to the Morrisites' religion later?

paragraphs.text: Many Morrisites, and many of their children, ended in the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints (now Community of Christ). The move came in waves over sixty years: soon after the siege in Utah and Idaho, then among George Williams's followers at Omaha, in Nevada and in California, then in Montana, and last among the young people of the Race Track church. Other Morrisites returned to the Latter-day Saint church.

Is there a monument at Kington Fort?

variants: Could Morrisite women hold the priesthood?
Did women hold the priesthood in Morris's church?
Were there Morrisite priestesses?
What was a High Priestess?
Did the Morrisites have women leaders?

paragraphs.text: Yes. A form "for ordaining an elect lady," signed by Joseph Morris and reported to Brigham Young's office in September 1861, anoints the woman "that thou mayest be an heiress of the Priesthood of Melchisedec." The title comes from Joseph Smith's revelation to Emma Smith. Morris was not the first leader after Nauvoo to open priesthood office to women: James J. Strang's Book of the Law of the Lord (1851) had already told his followers to "ordain teachers, men and women who are apt to teach."

The churches that followed George Williams ordained women as priestesses and High Priestesses. At Council Bluffs in 1869 Petronella Borgström was ordained a priestess "after Abel’s order", and at Omaha Williams called Marie Mortensen "High Priestess." In Montana, Margaret Thomas was reordained in 1872 "as the Lady elect to preside over the Female Order," and in 1890 two girls were ordained "to the lesser priesthood."
What a priestess or High Priestess could do outside the sisters' meetings is not yet clear.
